sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- coalition spokesman al-Maliki, via Anadolu T3 STATE (TR) + Arab News T3] Saudi air defences intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by the Ansar Allah toward the Riyadh region on Saturday Nov 7. No details on launch point, intended target within the Riyadh region, damage or casualties; coalition gave no imagery or debris. [CONTEXT] Second Riyadh attempt in ~12 hours: a drone was intercepted late Friday Nov 6 (recorded 0700-03). Friday morning also saw two ballistic missiles toward Najran and a drone over Mecca intercepted (recorded Nov 6). That is 5 coalition intercept claims in ~36 hours. The Ansar Allah have not claimed the cruise missile. [CONTEXT -- ISW Iran Update Nov 6] Ansar Allah may be concentrating forces in al Turbah for a large-scale offensive toward Aden; HOCC email transit-permit system normalizing control of Bab el-Mandeb (recorded 1400-02).
sections.what_verified: Coalition primary-source statement carried by 2 declared-tier families: Anadolu (T3, STATE TR) and Arab News (T3). Shafaq, Kurdistan24, Siasat, Yeni Safak, The Chronicle, The Pakistan Daily and GCC Scope carry the same statement but have NO declared tier in the registry -- attribution only, never counted. No independent confirmation of launch origin, interception, or debris; no Ansar Allah claim.
sections.what_disputed: No imagery, debris or independent verification of the launch or the intercept has been published (The Pakistan Daily notes this explicitly). The Ansar Allah have not claimed the launch. Secondary relays disagree on the sequence: Siasat dates BOTH the drone and the missile to Saturday Nov 7, while Arab News (updated 13:15) is explicit -- missile Saturday, drone late Friday; Arab News version used here. GCC Scope (untiered) adds unverified embellishments (civil-defence response, debris in residential zones, an Oct 30 date in its description) -- not used. No Saudi Press Agency standalone statement surfaced.
sections.why_matters: A cruise missile came for Riyadh itself -- the Saudi capital, 1,000 km from Yemen. Riyadh says it shot it down. It is the second strike on the capital in 12 hours -- and the Ansar Allah have not said a word about it.

totw_analysis: Our read: A cruise missile came for Riyadh itself -- the Saudi capital, 1,000 km from Yemen. Riyadh says it shot it down. It is the second strike on the capital in 12 hours -- and the Ansar Allah have not said a word about it. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Riyadh says its defences keep stopping everything -- a cruise missile now, a drone last night, missiles at Najran and Mecca on Friday. Residents ask why the alerts keep coming and whether the shield holds -- or is the capital now a routine target?
